summary: Reaching 7,145,000 English Wikipedia articles by 2026-03-01 would require about 145,000 new English articles in roughly 60 days (~2,417/day), far above the observed pace (~600/day).
Evidence indicates ~7,000,000 English articles by late 2025, suggesting that the base is large but growth signals are not sustaining a rapid near-term surge.
Bot-assisted growth could modestly boost near-term additions, but uncertainties around policy, quality controls, and deletions temper any potential spike.
Overall, the forecast probability is effectively near zero given the tight window and required growth rate.

question: Will the English Wikipedia have at least 7,145,000 articles before March 1, 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate is 1%, and the threshold requires adding 145,000 English-language articles in about 60 days, implying roughly 2,417 per day, which far exceeds near-term growth rates.

Adversarial objections correctly note possible upticks from bots, campaigns, or counting quirks, but the late-2025 baseline around 7 million English articles makes such a surge highly unlikely within the 60-day window.
Counting-method changes could marginally affect numbers but are unlikely to bridge the large gap to 7.145 million by 2026-03-01.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections correctly flag plausible upward drivers but the required rate to hit 7,145,000 by 2026-03-01 is implausible given late-2025 baselines and historical growth; thus the objections do not justify increasing the probability.
justification.adjustment: No adjustment; keeping the ensemble probability of 1% is warranted because the threshold breach is implausible under reported growth rates.

causal-factors.name: Required pace of growth to reach 7,145,000 English articles by 2026-03-01
causal-factors.rationale: To reach 145,000 more English articles in ~60 days would require about 2,417 new articles per day, roughly four times the ~600/day growth cited by multiple sources; given Dec 2025 English count around 7,000,000 and indications of plateauing, this is highly unlikely (Sources: Pew Research, December 2025; English Wikipedia milestone, May 2025).

causal-factors.rationale: If a major, sustained bot-driven or community effort produced many new English articles in Jan–Feb 2026, counts could rise more quickly, but there is no evidence in the provided sources; thus weak.

causal-factors.name: Counting methodology and deletions/merges affecting net article counts
causal-factors.rationale: Net article growth depends on both creation and deletion/merging to maintain quality; even as new articles are created, deletions and consolidations can keep net increases modest.

causal-factors.name: Growth-rate gap between current English Wikipedia article additions and the required pace to hit 7,145,000 by 2026-03-01
causal-factors.rationale: As of December 2025 English Wikipedia had about 7,000,000 articles; reaching 7,145,000 would require ~145,000 new articles in ~60 days, i.e., ~2,400 per day, far above the observed rate of roughly 600 new English articles per day.

causal-factors.name: Timeframe constraint (short 60-day window to 2026-03-01)
causal-factors.rationale: The 60-day window makes the required surge in article creation unlikely given current growth dynamics.

causal-factors.name: Milestone history and potential plateau after milestone (7,000,000 English articles reached May 28, 2025)
causal-factors.rationale: Milestones can be followed by slower growth, suggesting near-term gains into early 2026 may be more modest than earlier bursts.

causal-factors.name: Bot-assisted or automated article generation potential
causal-factors.rationale: Bots have accelerated article creation in some languages; if similar automation scales to English, net additions could modestly lift growth, though uncertainty remains.

causal-factors.name: Editorial and deletion dynamics (net growth tempered by deletions/merges)
causal-factors.rationale: Newly created articles can be deleted or merged during quality control, reducing net growth and challenging the target.

synthesis: The target is implausible given the short time window and historical growth rates, so the ensemble estimate remains the most plausible baseline. Objections identify potential upward nudges but do not materialize into a credible path to 7.145M by March 2026.
